8.heading: And thou hast:
refs: etc. Some render, "thou has fettered me," as kamat signifies in Arabic
but as it signifies in Syriac to be wrinkled, the common version seems, from the connexion, to be more correct
and if Job's disease were the elephantiasis, these words would apply most forcibly to the wrinkled state of the skin in that disorder.
8.body:
etc. Some render, "thou has fettered me," as kamat signifies in Arabic; but as it signifies in Syriac to be wrinkled, the common version seems, from the connexion, to be more correct; and if Job's disease were the elephantiasis, these words would apply most forcibly to the wrinkled state of the skin in that disorder.
